findings.title: Salesforce refresh writes credentials without importing prisma
findings.body: getClient now always calls prisma.credential.update after refreshing the Salesforce token, but prisma is never imported in this file. The first time a Salesforce calendar service is constructed, that reference throws ReferenceError and calendar create/update/delete all fail. The refresh also runs on every client construction even when the stored access token is still valid, so a transient token-endpoint failure now breaks Salesforce for the request instead of letting jsforce refresh lazily.

findings.title: Refreshed Salesforce token is not the one used
findings.body: After a successful token refresh, the new access token is written to the database, but the jsforce Connection is still constructed with credentialKey.access_token (the pre-refresh value) and credentialKey.instance_url. The in-memory client therefore keeps using the expired access token for the current booking/sync operation. This path also never goes through refreshOAuthTokens, so CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is ignored for Salesforce even when credential sharing is enabled.

findings.title: Google refresh persists the Zod parse wrapper as the credential
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a safeParse result ({ success, data }), but the Google refresh path stores that whole object in credential.key. Previously googleCredentialSchema.parse returned the token object itself. After the next token refresh, the stored key no longer matches googleCredentialSchema, so later Google Calendar calls fail schema parse and the real access/refresh tokens are overwritten in the database.

findings.title: Refresh parser injects a fake refresh token and cannot validate sync payloads
findings.body: If the parsed payload has no refresh_token, this helper sets refresh_token to the literal string "refresh_token" and returns it for callers to persist. Office 365 (and any provider that omits refresh_token on refresh) will overwrite the real refresh token with that placeholder, so the next refresh fails with invalid_grant. The sharing-mode schema is also wrong: computed keys are z.string().toString() / z.string().optional().toString() (strings like "ZodString"), not a catchall, and z.object strips unknown keys. Real sync responses therefore either fail validation or are saved without expiry_date, expires_in, and refresh_token.

findings.title: Sync refresh returns a raw fetch Response that callers cannot consume
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns the fetch Response and never reads JSON or checks response.ok. Callers were not updated to a single shape: Google reads res.data (axios-style), HubSpot/Zoho read .data.accessToken/.expiresIn/.error, and Lark/Webex/Zoom/Office pass the value to helpers that expect either a provider-specific JSON body or a Response whose JSON matches that provider. With sync on, token refresh throws or writes undefined tokens. The POST also sends no auth header and no Content-Type, so a typical JSON sync endpoint will not even accept the body.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sync sends credential id as the Cal user id
findings.body: refreshAccessToken calls refreshOAuthTokens with credentialId as the third argument, but that argument is documented and used as calcomUserId. When CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT is set, the parent app is asked for tokens for the wrong id (or no user), so Bigin refresh returns another user's tokens or fails, and those tokens can be stored on this credential.

findings.title: Zoom sync uses app slug zoomvideo instead of zoom
findings.body: Credential rows and the OAuth callback use appId "zoom", but refreshOAuthTokens is called with appSlug "zoomvideo". A sync endpoint that keys off the app slug used by the webhook (appMetadata.slug / "zoom") will not find the Zoom credential and will fail or return the wrong app's tokens during meeting creation.

findings.title: Credential webhook can create duplicate rows and has no error handling
findings.body: The handler does findFirst then create/update with no transaction or unique constraint. Concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user and app both see no row and insert two credentials; later findFirst updates only one, so calendar code that also uses findFirst can keep using a stale token. zod parse, symmetricDecrypt, and JSON.parse are uncaught, so a bad payload becomes an unstructured 500. The secret check is a plain !== (timing-leaky, and an array header value never matches).

findings.title: No tests for credential sync or the changed refresh paths
findings.body: The PR adds an unauthenticated-except-for-a-shared-secret endpoint that writes OAuth secrets, and it changes token refresh for Google, Office 365, Zoom, Salesforce, and others. The author notes tests were not added. There is no coverage that the webhook rejects a bad secret, decrypts and upserts a credential, or that a normal (sync disabled) refresh still persists a provider token object rather than a Zod wrapper or the string "refresh_token".
